America’s $40 trillion national debt sounds like a problem that should simply be paid off. But what if eliminating it could create an entirely different crisis?

This video explores the strange role U.S. government debt plays inside the global financial system. Treasury securities aren’t just IOUs sitting on a government balance sheet. Banks, pension funds, hedge funds, money market funds, and central banks use them as some of the world’s most important financial assets. They’re especially critical in the massive repo market, where trillions of dollars move between institutions using U.S. Treasuries as collateral. Remove enough of that collateral and the system could face serious liquidity problems.
